summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and weakness due to hypercalcemia in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He received pamidronate in clinic prior to admission, which resolved his hypercalcemia. During his stay, he was treated with a 4-day pulse of dexamethasone followed by a new regimen of dexamethasone, Velcade, and Cytoxan due to progression of myeloma. His hospital course was complicated by steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring insulin drip and dose adjustments, and poorly controlled hypertension managed with increased diltiazem and addition of amlodipine. Acute kidney injury, likely from hypercalcemia and dehydration, improved from a creatinine of 1.7 to 1.3. Dyspnea was attributed to anemia, and he was transfused one unit of red blood cells with symptom improvement. He remained on oral vancomycin for C. diff prevention and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in oncology, endocrinology, and cardiology.
